newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Barclay chief wants EMU to be postponed.
newsitem.headline: Barclay chief wants EMU to be postponed.

text.p: Barclays Plc Chief Executive Martin Taylor said Germany's budget woes and the Left's strong gains in the first round of French elections made European Economic and Monertary Union less likely to start on time.

"I think there is a much lower chance of EMU happening on time today than there was 10 days ago. More worryingly, there is a much higher chance of a bad EMU happening," he said, calling for the 1999 start date to be put back. He cited the danger of politicians manipulating the single currency project to fit political considerations, undermining the currency.
He said there was a danger of a French government coming into power with "a fantasy agenda" and noted "increasing distrust among the German population for what is happening."

"If governments against this background do try to fix the currencies it is the duty of currency speculators to blow them apart," he said. "I think by doing that they would do the world a very good turn."
He hoped EMU would be postponed until it could have a more favourable environment.

"The earlier the postponement comes the more credible it will be," he said. "A confident, strong, statesmanslike postponement early will give a good chance of a healthy EMU in three, four or five years time."
